title: Runbook execution sandbox and safety mesh for interactive admin utilities
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a hardened sandbox and safety mesh for executing runbooks-as-tasks used by oncall and support engineers. Purpose: allow safe dry-run, replay, and policy-enforced live execution of admin utilities with step-level permission gating and automatic idempotency checks. This ticket scopes the initial runtime integration, an eventing surface for telemetry, and a minimal policy engine that enforces allowed step actions per role. The deliverable is a developer-facing sandbox endpoint (ops-sandbox) plus a safety mesh library injected into the runbook runtime to validate and optionally block steps before they reach production connectors.
acceptance_criteria: Ops-sandbox endpoint that accepts a runbook bundle JSON and returns a deterministic dry-run trace without invoking external services
Safety mesh policy evaluation runs for every step with user/role context and can block steps tagged 'dangerous'
Rewind-and-replay: preserved trace with UUIDs for each step and ability to replay up to a step boundary in staging
Idempotency checker flags non-idempotent actions and suggests mutation wrappers
Per-step telemetry emitted (event ids, duration, result, blocked_reason) to the runbook-telemetry stream
E2E test harness that simulates a synthetic incident and validates safe-fail behavior under quota and permission failures
comments: 2026-02-28 Aisha Patel: Created initial PRD and linked the prototype harness. Goal is not to replace the full runbook orchestration but to provide a safety-first developer surface for incremental rollout.

2026-03-10 Marcus Chen: Drafted telemetry schema and pushed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-runbooks/pull/468 (WIP). Requires instrumentation library change in runtime-1.21 branch.

2026-03-12 Aisha Patel: Decided to gate 'network egress' and 'infra-critical' step types behind a separate allowlist managed in console. Action: PM to add admin panel for allowlist management (see links).
notes: Implementation approach: instrument the existing runbook runner with a pluggable 'safety-mesh' filter chain. The sandbox will execute against in-memory service emulators (secrets redacted).
Trade-offs considered: full emulation fidelity vs. speed. We will start with a deterministic emulator for common connectors (k8s, sql, vault) and expand based on incidents encountered.
Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout to internal oncall, then opt-in for SRE teams, then org-wide after 2-week stabilization window.
Telemetry plan: use runbook-telemetry stream with event types: step.start, step.end, step.blocked, step.replay. Include trace_id and step_id for correlate with logs.
Test plan: create three synthetic incident scenarios (stateful DB migration, token rotation, pod restart) to validate dry-run fidelity and safe-failures.
Open question: whether to surface automatic remediation suggestions. For MVP we will only flag and annotate; suggestions are a follow-up ticket.
